title: Start, stop, restart, or check status of a service
summary: Control the state of a specific systemd service. You can start, stop, restart, reload, or check the current status of any service unit.

steps.explain: Use systemctl with the desired action (start, stop, restart, reload, or status) and the name of the service unit.

placeholders.name: ACTION
placeholders.description: The action to perform: start, stop, restart, reload, or status.

placeholders.name: UNIT
placeholders.description: The name of the service unit (e.g., nginx.service or sshd).

rollback.explain: To undo a stop or restart, start the service again. To undo a start, stop it.

placeholders.name: OPPOSITE_ACTION
placeholders.description: The opposite action: if you stopped it, use start; if you started it, use stop.

placeholders.name: UNIT
placeholders.description: The name of the service unit.

warnings: Stopping a critical service (like ssh or display manager) may disconnect you or close your session.
